title: Different tastes within a fair choice

captions.physics: Agreeing clear terms for shared enjoyment
captions.energy: Seeking equal strength of shared desire

meaning: Shared leisure can combine different tastes when a fair agreement does not require equal desire or an identical impression at every step.
text: A fair choice can include two people without their tastes matching completely. Justice in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps agree on time, conditions and each person’s right to suggest something pleasant. The Lovers in energy lean towards seeking equally strong desire, as though enjoyment otherwise were not fully shared. Temperance in emotions allows differences to feel capable of joining within a suitable rhythm. Agreement needs to serve actual preferences alongside outward equality: equal time alone cannot reveal what either wants now.

For example, you choose a food tasting with different sauces. One person enjoys spicy flavours while the other wants to linger over something mild. **Agreed enjoyment can combine different preferences.** You can divide portions by preference, beyond halving every one, and exchange impressions. Free agreement preserves fairness while differences create harmony. There is something for both to share without equally loving every flavour or displaying identical enthusiasm for the whole programme.

The difficulty is correcting difference through more precise distribution. You divide everything equally, check whether it was sufficiently enjoyable and miss pleasure giving way to assessment. Ensuring unity interferes with coordination. Temperance need not erase individual wishes. It helps them meet when fairness permits flexible participation instead of requiring feelings to follow a prior arithmetic, as though numbers could guarantee enjoyment for both.
